title: Israel's deputy FM, Sharren Haskel, bets on a new right after breaking with Netanyahu
gist: Sharren Haskel resigned as Israel's deputy foreign minister and quit New Hope over legislation exempting ultra-Orthodox men from military service, launching a new 'Israel First' party aimed at forming a centrist Zionist bloc ahead of the October 27 elections, while continuing to back Netanyahu's West Bank settlement policy, close US ties, and the Israel-Lebanon disarmament framework.

themes.theme: New 'Israel First' party and election bet

insights.claim: Sharren Haskel resigned as deputy foreign minister and quit the New Hope party on July 14, then formed a new party, Israel First, which she is confident will win enough votes to enter the Knesset in the October 27, 2026 elections.
insights.speaker: Rina Bassist
insights.so_what: A new party entering an already fragmented Knesset race adds uncertainty to Israel's October 27 election outcome and coalition math.
insights.locator: Two weeks after resigning as deputy foreign minister

insights.claim: Haskel says Israel First will be the only Knesset party led by a woman, positioning her identity as a young, Mizrahi, female combat-veteran mother as a distinct political asset.
insights.speaker: Rina Bassist
insights.so_what: Signals the identity-based positioning Israel First will use to differentiate itself in a crowded right-of-center field.
insights.quote: I'm a woman. I'm young. I'm Mizrahi, of Moroccan descent. I served as a combat soldier, and I'm proud of it
insights.locator: Haskel told Al-Monitor, stressing that her party

insights.claim: Haskel says she is trying to build a right-wing bloc 'free from political extortion' that would force Netanyahu, Yashar leader Gadi Eisenkot, and Together leader Naftali Bennett to sit together and build a platform around Israel's security, economy and national unity.
insights.speaker: Rina Bassist
insights.so_what: Names the specific rival right-of-center leaders Haskel wants to force into coalition, a concrete post-election scenario for investors modeling Israeli political stability.
insights.quote: I want to create a bloc that will force Netanyahu and [Yashar leader Gadi] Eisenkot, Netanyahu and [Together leader Naftali] Bennett, to sit together and build a platform focused on Israel's security, its economy and national unity.
insights.locator: I'm in discussions with many people

insights.claim: Haskel argues that a right-wing government is currently 'held hostage' by ultra-Orthodox parties just as a left-wing government would be held hostage by Arab parties, and that her movement aims to build a governing bloc in the middle free of both.
insights.speaker: Rina Bassist
insights.so_what: Frames the structural coalition problem — small sectoral parties holding disproportionate leverage — that Haskel's party is explicitly designed to break.
insights.quote: Today, a right-wing government is held hostage by the ultra-Orthodox parties. A left-wing government would be held hostage by the Arab parties.
insights.locator: Today, a right-wing government is held hostage

insights.claim: Haskel resigned from the government over coalition-backed legislation that shields ultra-Orthodox men who evade military service from arrest, which she called 'legally and morally corrupt, especially during wartime.'
insights.speaker: Rina Bassist
insights.so_what: Identifies the ultra-Orthodox draft-exemption legislation as the specific trigger for a senior minister's resignation and new-party formation, marking it as a live fault line in Israeli coalition politics.
insights.quote: This exemption law is legally and morally corrupt, especially during wartime. That's why I was so furious

insights.claim: According to Israeli military data published July 28, about 4,000 ultra-Orthodox men aged 18-26 enlisted over the prior 12 months, while roughly 14,000 ultra-Orthodox men reach draft age each year and about 80,000 are currently eligible for military service.
insights.speaker: Rina Bassist
insights.so_what: Quantifies the scale of the ultra-Orthodox draft-evasion gap (roughly 4,000 enlisted versus ~80,000 eligible), the core statistic underlying the political fight over exemption legislation.
insights.locator: According to Israeli military data published July 28

insights.claim: Haskel predicts Israel's Supreme Court will likely reject the ultra-Orthodox exemption bill because the government itself knows it is legally and morally indefensible, given that nearly 20 Knesset members are ultra-Orthodox with family members who could otherwise be wanted by military police for draft evasion.
insights.speaker: Rina Bassist
insights.so_what: A likely Supreme Court rejection of the exemption law would reopen the coalition's central fault line regardless of the election outcome.
insights.quote: The Supreme Court will probably reject this bill and cancel it. The government knows it cannot defend it because it's indefensible from both legal and moral points of view.
insights.locator: The Supreme Court will probably reject this bill

insights.claim: Haskel says Israel-US strategic cooperation remains very close despite her disagreements with Netanyahu on some issues, framing Trump's war with Iran as defending American interests in parallel with Israel defending its own.
insights.speaker: Rina Bassist
insights.so_what: A senior Israeli political figure publicly affirming close US-Israel alignment despite friction with Netanyahu suggests the strategic relationship is durable even amid domestic Israeli political upheaval.
insights.quote: The cooperation between Israel and the US is very close. We know that America is our ally.
insights.locator: I have some disagreements with Netanyahu on certain issues

insights.claim: Haskel says Israel endured six months of bombardment by Hezbollah and the Iranian military before responding, framing this restraint as evidence Israel is not the aggressor in the broader conflict.
insights.speaker: Rina Bassist
insights.so_what: Provides an official Israeli political narrative timeline (six months of bombardment before retaliation) useful for tracking how Israeli leaders justify the broader Middle East war to allies.
insights.quote: Israel had been attacked for six months, bombarded by Hezbollah and the Iranian military, before we responded. No other country would have tolerated that.
insights.locator: Israel had been attacked for six months

insights.claim: Haskel says the Lebanese military faces a significant problem because personnel affiliated with or related to Hezbollah serve in its ranks, but that the June 26 Israel-Lebanon agreement offers Lebanon a one-time opportunity to break from Iranian patronage, adding that neither Israel nor the US intend to remain in south Lebanon forever.
insights.speaker: Rina Bassist
insights.so_what: A senior Israeli official conditioning withdrawal on Lebanese army reliability signals the pace of Israel's south Lebanon pullback will hinge on perceived de-Hezbollahization progress, not a fixed timetable.
insights.quote: the June 26 agreement between Israel and Lebanon offers the Lebanese people a one-time opportunity to liberate themselves from their Iranian patrons
insights.locator: The Lebanese military is facing a significant problem
